categories.main_business_segments: i-mobile operates two main business segments: the Consumer Business, centered on the 'Furunavi' hometown tax donation platform and related services (travel, restaurant PR, and points), and the Internet Advertising Business, which includes ad network, influencer marketing, media solutions, agency, and app operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary digital platforms for ad distribution (including multi-device ad networks and full-screen video ads), advanced data analytics, and automated systems for matching advertisers and media. In the Consumer Business, robust web-based systems manage donation processing, user engagement, and seamless integration with travel and restaurant services.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include local governments (for the hometown tax platform), individual consumers (donors and users of travel/restaurant/points services), advertisers, media companies, app developers, and corporate clients seeking influencer or digital marketing solutions. The main end markets are Japanese consumers and businesses engaged in digital marketing.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company primarily operates in Japan, with nearly all revenue and assets located domestically. Past overseas subsidiaries in the US and Taiwan have been dissolved, and current activities are focused on the Japanese market.
categories.supply_chain_position: i-mobile is positioned downstream in the digital marketing supply chain, acting as an intermediary between advertisers and media/app publishers, and as a platform operator directly interfacing with end-users and local governments in the Consumer Business.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding user acquisition and engagement, developing new businesses leveraging existing assets (especially around 'Furunavi'), diversifying revenue streams, and strengthening technology and development capabilities (including AI and system stability). The company also emphasizes sustainability, regional revitalization, and M&A for growth.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through transaction-based fees and commissions: platform fees from local governments for hometown tax donations, advertising fees from advertisers (performance-based and impression-based), and service fees from corporate clients for influencer marketing and media solutions. App operations generate revenue via in-app advertising and user engagement.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other digital marketing firms, ad networks, and hometown tax portal operators. i-mobile is a leading player in both the hometown tax donation platform market (targeting a 20% share) and is one of the largest domestic ad networks, though it faces strong competition from both domestic and global digital platforms.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending July 2025, consolidated revenue was 21.5 billion yen (up 14.9% YoY), with operating profit of 4.1 billion yen and net profit of 3.0 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth in both revenue and profit, with a strong balance sheet and high ROE (18.7%). The Consumer Business is the main growth driver.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: i-mobile differentiates itself through its integrated digital platforms, strong technology and operational expertise, and ability to deliver high ROI for advertisers and high convenience for users. In the Consumer Business, unique features such as seamless travel booking with tax donations and a broad ecosystem of services enhance user engagement and regional impact. In advertising, the company emphasizes scale, multi-device compatibility, and one-stop solutions.
